research.createthaumaresearch.unlock_mec: My arcane devices run on vis. But a waterwheel turns without vis, and a mill grinds without it. There may be a craft of machines that needs no magic at all, only motion.
Motion, metal and order: Mechanoturgy is its own discipline now, with a chapter of its own.
research.createthaumaresearch.base_mecha: Andesite, bound with iron, holds a shape the way living stone never does. It is the first material of machines that need no vis: an alloy that does not tire, a key that turns them.
research.createthaumaresearch.kinetics.s: Everything around me moves: water runs, a pendulum swings, a cart rolls. Motion can be watched, and what can be watched can be understood.
A turning rod passes its motion on, a toothed wheel hands it to the next. With a crank I can be the first mover myself; cased in andesite, the turning is safe to stand beside.
research.createthaumaresearch.water_powe: A river never rests. If a wheel stood in its way, the river would turn it for me, day and night, asking nothing.
Paddles on a wheel, the wheel on a shaft: falling and flowing water now turn my machines. The larger the wheel, the slower and stronger it turns.
research.createthaumaresearch.wind_power: Aer is the most restless of the primals. Where water must be led, wind comes by itself.
A bearing that turns whatever is fixed to it, and sails to catch the wind: a whole structure becomes one great rotor.
research.createthaumaresearch.transmissi: Turning carries something, the way a current carries essentia. It can be bent around corners, sped up or slowed down, and every machine takes its share.
A large wheel against a small one changes the speed; a box of gears turns the motion aside; a belt or a chain carries it far.
My goggles of revealing show me the aspects of things, but not how hard a shaft strains. Another lens is needed.
Engineer's goggles show speed and stress at a glance; dials on the shaft show them to anyone passing by.
research.createthaumaresearch.signals.st: A machine that cannot be stopped is a danger. The relay taught me how redstone can carry a will across a distance.
A clutch cuts the motion, a gearshift reverses it, a link carries a signal through the air. Boards and tubes tell me what my machines are doing.
research.createthaumaresearch.tools.stag: Iron and motion together make a tool that never grows tired in the hand.
A drill that bites stone, a saw that fells trees, a harvester and a plough: the shaft does the work my arms used to.
research.createthaumaresearch.processing: Rotation and a tool add up to a mechanism. Machina is the spark that makes the iron seem alive.
A press that flattens, a mixer that stirs a basin, a millstone that grinds, a fan that blows through fire or water: the crafts of the workshop, done by turning.
Things must move too, not only shafts. A hungry chest swallows what is thrown at it; I want things to go where I send them.
Belts and chutes carry, funnels take and give, a vault holds what a hundred chests would, and an ejector throws things across the room.
research.createthaumaresearch.brass.stag: I make brass in the crucible from a nugget and an aspect. The mixer makes it from copper and zinc, with heat and patience. The metal is the same; the road is not.
Brass cases the finer machines, and a tube of rose quartz carries a signal through them.
research.createthaumaresearch.blaze_heat: The Infernal Furnace taught me that the Nether keeps a better fire. A blaze, caged and fed, would keep it burning under my basin.
An empty burner waits for a blaze. Fed with fuel, it heats the basin above for mixing and pressing that ordinary fire cannot do.
research.createthaumaresearch.fluids.sta: Essentia flows through my tubes by suction. Water, lava and honey could flow the same way, pushed by a turning pump instead.
Pipes, a pump and tanks; a spout to fill, a drain to empty, a pulley to drink a lake dry.
research.createthaumaresearch.steam.stag: Fire and water together make steam, and steam pushes harder than any river.
A tank over blaze burners becomes a boiler; engines on its sides turn a great flywheel. A whistle tells how hard it works.
research.createthaumaresearch.smog.title: Overload and Smog
research.createthaumaresearch.smog.stage: My boilers work day and night, and the air around them has changed. Too much fuel and too much turning throw off something worse than smoke: flux. Where flux gathers, the taint follows. I must keep my machines in measure.
research.createthaumaresearch.sorting.st: Golems know which item is which because I put a seal on them. A brass funnel could know it too, if I gave it a filter.
Filters choose, brass funnels and tunnels obey them, and a mechanical arm picks things up and puts them down where they belong.
My complex mechanism is made by hand, gear by gear. A row of machines could put one together the same way, step after step.
A deployer uses what it holds as a hand would; crafters work as one big crafting table; a controller sets the speed exactly.
research.createthaumaresearch.contraptio: My levitator lifts things, but lets them fall. A piston could carry a whole wall and set it down where I want it.
Pistons push, pulleys lift, carriages slide along a shaft; glue and chassis hold the blocks together while they travel.
research.createthaumaresearch.schematics: A building is a pattern, the same way a research note is. If I could write the pattern down, a machine could read it and build.
The quill draws a schematic, the table copies it, and the schematicannon fires blocks into place one by one.
research.createthaumaresearch.trains.sta: A moving structure that follows a track could cross the world. A train is a contraption that goes somewhere.
Tracks and stations, signals that keep trains apart, controls and a schedule for a train that drives itself.
Golems carry what I ask for. A network of machines could do the same: wrap the goods, send them, and keep count of what is left.
A packager wraps, a frogport sends and receives, the stock ticker counts and orders, and factory gauges keep a whole workshop supplied.
